prompt: Match each blocked reply to the layer that blocked it.
hint: One layer on the right blocked nothing.

pairs.left: r3, the marker from the system prompt

prompt: Why does each block name the layer that made it?
hint: Who reads the log after a complaint?

choices.text: Because the client is shown the name of the layer
choices.why: The name is for whoever reads the log, not for the client.

choices.text: So the model learns which layer to avoid
choices.why: Nothing is fed back to the model here.

choices.text: Because layers are billed separately
choices.why: Cost is not why.

choices.text: So a complaint reaches the right layer
choices.why: Right.

prompt: Which rules decide the order of the chain at Tarefa? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Layers that may signal an incident go first
choices.why: Yes: the record must say so.

choices.text: Cheap checks before expensive ones
choices.why: Yes: a blocked reply need not be scored.

choices.text: The same chain on every path a reply can take
choices.why: Yes: a second route is a way around.

choices.text: The layer with the fewest false positives goes last
choices.why: No such rule was given.

prompt: A daily e-mail summary of the assistant's conversations is sent to clients without the filter chain. What does the lesson say about it?

choices.text: It is fine, since the replies were filtered when first shown
choices.why: The summary is new text and a new path.

choices.text: It is a way around every layer, so it needs the chain
choices.why: Right: the same chain on every path.

choices.text: It only needs moderation, since it is a summary
choices.why: A summary can carry a CPF or a link as well as anything.

choices.text: It should be sent to staff instead, who do not need filters
choices.why: The issue is the clients who receive it.

prompt: With all four layers on, how many of the six replies pass?
What does it mean that a denylist fails open?

choices.text: What it did not foresee passes
choices.why: Right: the zero cut the score from 0.84 to 0.60.

choices.text: It refuses values nobody forbade
choices.why: That is how an allowlist fails.

choices.text: It stops working when the list is empty
choices.why: An empty denylist passes everything, which is the same failure taken to its end.

choices.text: It opens a connection to the moderation provider
choices.why: Nothing about networks.

prompt: Why was `photography` refused, though nobody wrote it down as forbidden?
hint: Which kind of list is the category rule?

choices.text: Photography jobs break Tarefa's terms of use
choices.why: Nothing says so; it is simply not on the list.

choices.text: The moderation layer scored it as spam
choices.why: Moderation does not read the category.

choices.text: An allowlist refuses whatever it does not name
choices.why: Right: it fails closed, and the fix is to add the value.

choices.text: The input was longer than the field allows
choices.why: It is one word.

prompt: When is a denylist the right choice, according to the lesson?
hint: Can every good value be listed?

choices.text: Always, because it never blocks a legitimate value
choices.why: It lets through what it did not foresee.

choices.text: When the good values are open-ended, as in free text
choices.why: Right: and then it is a signal, with a person on the doubtful band.

choices.text: When the list of bad values is longer than the list of good ones
choices.why: Length is not the test.

choices.text: For hosts, since bad hosts are easier to list
choices.why: Nobody can list every bad host before it appears; hosts take an allowlist.

prompt: Match each mechanism to what it does.
hint: One description on the right belongs to none of them.

pairs.right: Names what is refused, and lets through what it did not foresee
Names what is accepted, and refuses whatever it does not name
Decides the doubtful band a denylist leaves open

right_distractors: Decides which layer of the chain runs first

prompt: What does a reply containing `CANARY-7F3A-TAREFA` tell the team?

choices.text: The client typed the marker into the chat
choices.why: Clients never see the marker; it is only in the system prompt.

choices.text: The model leaked a credential
choices.why: The marker is not a credential; it means nothing.

choices.text: The reply repeated the system prompt
choices.why: Right: so it is blocked and somebody is alerted.

choices.text: The moderation layer has failed
choices.why: Moderation is a different layer.

prompt: `r6` describes the system prompt's instructions in its own words and passes. What does that show?
hint: What exactly does a canary look for?

choices.text: A canary catches the verbatim leak, not a paraphrase
choices.why: Right: a paraphrase does not carry the marker.

choices.text: r6 is not a leak, since it is paraphrased
choices.why: It describes the instructions; whether that matters depends on what they contain.

choices.text: The canary layer was switched off for r6
choices.why: r6 passed in both runs, with the canary on and off.

choices.text: Paraphrases are blocked by moderation instead
choices.why: Moderation scores abuse, not leaks.

prompt: Which practices does the lesson give for canaries? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: One marker per prompt version
choices.why: Yes: an alert then says which version leaked.

choices.text: Never rely on the canary to protect a secret in the prompt
choices.why: Yes: it reports a leak and prevents none.

choices.text: Write the system prompt as if it will be read
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Tell clients the marker so they can report it
choices.why: Then it would appear in replies for innocent reasons.

prompt: A marker that means nothing, written into the system prompt so that its appearance in a reply reveals a leak, is called a ___.
Put the layers of the lab's chain in the order they run.
hint: Incident signals first, the network call later, links last.

prompt: A team proposes replacing the whole chain with one strong moderation model. What is the lesson's objection?
hint: Read the last column of the table.

choices.text: Moderation models are too slow for chat
choices.why: Speed is not the objection.

choices.text: One layer keeps every miss the others would catch
choices.why: Right: a CPF, a canary and a lookalike host are not moderation categories.

choices.text: Moderation models are forbidden by the LGPD
choices.why: No such rule.

choices.text: A strong model never makes mistakes, so the chain is redundant
choices.why: No model is perfect, and the categories do not cover these cases anyway.
